sentences.text:
The following arguments made by Shri Hanuman Deen Verma, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by ShriShashi Dhar Pandey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 14 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victim in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as15 yearsare unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is15 years and 10 monthsof age.
(iv)The medical report drawn up as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol to determine the age of the victim opines that she is 18 years of age.
The victim is in fact a major.
3. Briefly put the prosecution case in the FIR is that the principal offender one Mukesh had enticed the minor daughters of the informant and had eloped with them.
4. The applicant was not named in the FIR.
5. The FIR arises out of a relationship between the victim and the principal offender Mukesh.
6. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has admitted to accompanying the principal offender Mukesh to Sant Kabir Nagar, Gorakhpur and thereon to Lucknow.
Lastly, the three persons went to Delhi.
7. By and large the victim has reiterated the aforesaid version in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
In the latter statement the victim has added that she had made consensual physical relations with the applicant.

8. It is noteworthy that the victim has not made any allegation of abduction, unlawful confinement,
assault or rape against the applicant in either of the statements.

sentences.text: The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places.
She did not raise an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party.
10. Major inconsistencies in the F.I.R. statements of the victim under Sections 180 B.N.S. and 183 B.N.S. discredit the prosecution case.
11. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Akshya be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
